0.headline: Milky Mist raises over Rs 465 crore via anchor book ahead of Rs 1,553-crore IPO; Temasek buys more shares
0.heading: Milky Mist raises over Rs 465 crore via anchor book ahead of Rs 1,553-crore IPO; Temasek buys more shares
0.intro: Milky Mist IPO | Singaporean investment firm Temasek Holdings emerged as the largest buyer in the company through the anchor book.
0.body:
Chennai-based dairy products maker Milky Mist Dairy Food has raised Rs 465.3 crore from 19 anchor investors on August 10, a day before the IPO opens for public subscription.

The company tapped the capital markets to raise up to Rs 1,553 crore through an initial public offering (IPO) at the upper end of the price band of Rs 133-140 per share. The IPO comprises a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 1,428 crore, while promoter Sathishkumar T and his wife, Anitha S, will sell shares worth Rs 125 crore through an offer-for-sale (OFS).

The issue will open for public subscription on August 11 and close on August 13, 2026.

Milky Mist Dairy Food on Monday finalised the allocation of 3.32 crore equity shares through the anchor book at the upper end of the price band.

Singaporean investment firm Temasek Holdings emerged as the largest buyer in the company through the anchor book. Its subsidiary Zulia Investments Pte picked up 1.14 crore equity shares worth Rs 160 crore (equivalent to 1.48 percent of post issue paid-up equity), while International Finance Corporation bought 14.28 lakh shares for Rs 20 crore.

Temasek, through Jongsong Investments Pte, already held a 5.16 percent stake in Milky Mist, which was acquired in the pre-IPO round.

Out of the total allocation of 3.32 crore equity shares to anchor investors, the company allocated 1.53 crore shares to nine domestic mutual funds, including Nippon Life India, HDFC AMC, ICICI Prudential AMC, Invesco MF, Motilal Oswal AMC, Edelweiss, HSBC Mutual Fund, Union MF and Trust AMC, which applied through their 13 schemes, Milky Mist said in its filing with the exchanges.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Among others, IIFL Asset Management, India Acorn Fund and Anicut Equity Continuum Fund also invested in the company through the anchor book. Aditya Birla Sun Life Insurance was allocated 7.14 lakh shares worth Rs 10 crore by the company.

Milky Mist, which makes cheese, paneer, butter, curd, ghee, yogurt, ice cream and ultra-high-temperature long-shelf-life products, will utilise Rs 496.8 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue to repay debt, while Rs 469.2 crore will be spent on the expansion and modernisation of its Perundurai manufacturing facility.

Further, the company will use Rs 155.3 crore for the deployment of visi coolers, ice cream freezers and chocolate coolers, with the remainder being utilised for general corporate purposes.

As of May 2026, Milky Mist had consolidated outstanding borrowings of Rs 1,390.7 crore.

The company offers all its products under the umbrella brand Milky Mist, as well as multiple sub-brands such as SmartChef, Capella and Misty Lite. It operates from a single manufacturing facility in Perundurai, Tamil Nadu.

JM Financial, Axis Capital and IIFL Capital Services are acting as the merchant bankers for the Milky Mist IPO.

1.headline: Shankesh Jewellers IPO to Dalal Street on August 18, likely to raise Rs 370 crore
1.heading: Shankesh Jewellers IPO to Dalal Street on August 18, likely to raise Rs 370 crore
1.intro: Shankesh Jewellers IPO | The initial public offering of 3.94 crore equity shares comprises a fresh issue of 2.94 crore shares and an offer-for-sale of 1 crore shares.
1.body:
Shankesh Jewellers, the Mumbai-based B2B manufacturer and distributor of handcrafted gold jewellery, will launch its maiden public issue worth nearly Rs 370 crore next week on August 18.

This will be the second mainboard IPO to open next week, following Lalithaa Jewellery Mart on August 17.

Shankesh Jewellers' initial public offering (IPO) of 3.94 crore equity shares comprises a fresh issue of 2.94 crore shares and an offer-for-sale (OFS) of 1 crore shares.

Promoters Kantilal Kheemraj Jain and his son Manoj Kantilal Jain will be the selling shareholders in the offer-for-sale.

The company has reserved 50 percent of the offer size for qualified institutional buyers (QIBs), while 35 percent of the shares have been allocated to the retail category and the remaining 15 percent to non-institutional investors.

The price band for the public issue will be announced on August 11.

The IPO anchor book will open on August 17, while the offer will close for public subscription on August 20. The company is expected to finalise the IPO share allotment by August 21 and list its equity shares on the stock exchanges on August 25.

Click Here To Read All IPO News

Shankesh Jewellers manufactures handcrafted gold jewellery in 22-karat and 18-karat gold through third-party job workers for several clients, including Joyalukkas India, P N Gadgil &amp; Sons, Kalyan Jewellers India, P N Gadgil Jewellers, Manoj Vaibhav Gems ‘N’ Jewellers, and Novel Jewels (Aditya Birla Group), among others.

The company intends to utilise Rs 158 crore of the net proceeds from the fresh issue to repay loans, Rs 38 crore to meet its working capital requirements, and the remainder for general corporate purposes.

As of June 2026, its working capital facilities stood at Rs 167 crore, while outstanding borrowings stood at Rs 162.94 crore. This means the company will significantly reduce its debt post-IPO.

Shankesh Jewellers, which operates under an asset-light business model, reported a profit of Rs 106.7 crore for the year ended March 2026, up 164.6 percent from Rs 40.3 crore in the previous year. Revenue from operations increased 16.2 percent to Rs 1,630.8 crore from Rs 1,403.8 crore during the same period.

Aryaman Financial Services and Smart Horizon Capital Advisors are the merchant bankers managing the Shankesh Jewellers IPO.

2.headline: Shiprocket IPO GMP rises to 28% ahead of August 12 issue opening; check lot size, timeline and key details
2.heading: Shiprocket IPO GMP rises to 28% ahead of August 12 issue opening; check lot size, timeline and key details
2.intro: Shiprocket’s shares are commanding a strong premium in the grey market ahead of the company’s initial public offering (IPO), with the latest grey market premium (GMP) indicating a potential listing gain of nearly 28 percent over the upper end of the issue price band.
2.body:
Shiprocket’s shares are commanding a strong premium in the grey market ahead of the company’s initial public offering (IPO), with the latest grey market premium (GMP) indicating a potential listing gain of nearly 28 percent over the upper end of the issue price band.

According to InvestorGain, Shiprocket’s GMP stood at Rs 26.50 per share on August 10, translating into a 27.32 percent premium over the upper price band of Rs 97. IPO Watch has also pegged the GMP at 27.32 percent.

However, investors should note that GMP is an unofficial indicator derived from the grey market and is not regulated. It can change before listing and does not guarantee listing gains or indicate the underlying fundamentals of the company.

Read Also: School dropout to founder of Rs 10,000 crore company: How IPO-bound Milky Mist's Sathish Kumar went from selling 10 kg paneer to building a dairy giant

Shiprocket has fixed the price band for its IPO at Rs 92-97 per share. The Rs 1,617.48 crore issue comprises a fresh issue of Rs 885.50 crore and an offer for sale of Rs 731.98 crore. The company is seeking a market capitalisation of Rs 7,057.5 crore at the upper end of the price band.

The IPO will open for subscription on August 12 and close on August 14. The anchor book is scheduled to open on August 11. The basis of allotment is expected on August 17, while the shares are scheduled to list on the BSE and NSE on August 19, subject to changes.

The Gurugram-based company is backed by investors including Bertelsmann, Temasek, Tribe Capital and Eternal. Existing shareholders, including Lightrock, Tribe Capital and other investors, will sell shares through the OFS component.

For eligible employees, the company has offered a discount of Rs 9 per share to the final issue price. Shares worth Rs 1 crore have been reserved for the employee portion.

The minimum bid is 154 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 14,938 at the upper end of the price band. Retail investors can bid for up to 2,002 shares, or 13 lots, translating into a maximum application amount of Rs 1,94,194.

Check IPO News Here

The issue has reserved not less than 75 percent of the net offer for qualified institutional buyers, not more than 15 percent for non-institutional investors and not more than 10 percent for retail investors.

Shiprocket plans to deploy Rs 365.6 crore from the fresh issue towards investments in the growth of its platforms. This includes spending on marketing initiatives and technology infrastructure and capabilities.

Another Rs 210 crore has been earmarked for repayment or prepayment of certain borrowings. The remaining proceeds will be used for funding inorganic growth through unidentified acquisitions and general corporate purposes.

The company had total borrowings of Rs 242.01 crore as of March 31, 2026, according to its restated consolidated financials.

Shiprocket continued to report losses in FY26, although the deficit remained substantially below the level recorded in FY24.

The company reported a consolidated loss after tax of Rs 79.25 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 74.45 crore in FY25 and Rs 595.18 crore in FY24. Total income increased to Rs 2,077.42 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,674.82 crore in FY25, representing growth of about 24 percent.

About Shiprocket

Shiprocket operates a technology-enabled e-commerce platform offering logistics, fulfilment, payments, checkout, customer engagement and cross-border commerce solutions to MSMEs, D2C brands and larger enterprises. The company has expanded beyond its original shipping and logistics business into areas such as warehousing, fulfilment, international shipping, digital marketing and payments.
